title: Protocol to downregulate GABAergic-astrocyte signaling via astrocyte-selective ablation of GABAB receptor in adult mice
protocol: Use Gabbr1-floxed mice aged 3–4 months for generating transgenic mice.
Inject mice with adenoviral particles expressing Cre recombinase in mPFC astrocytes (AVV2.5-GFAP-Cre-mCherry, viral titer 4.3 × 10^12 vg/mL).
Weigh mice prior to anesthesia.
Inject 0.1 mg per kg of buprenorphine subcutaneously.
Anesthetize mice with isoflurane (1.5–2% in O₂).
Place the animal in the stereotaxic frame once anesthetized.
Put a heating pad below to maintain body temperature at approximately 36°C.
Fix the mouse’s head placing the ear bars of the stereotaxic frame in front of the ears.
Cover the eyes with eye gel to avoid dryness.
Shave the animal’s head with a razor blade.
Apply ethanol and an antiseptic (Betadine or similar) with a cotton bud.
Make an incision from back to front with scissors.
Remove tissue above the skull using cotton buds and forceps.
Take stereotaxic coordinates.
Place the tip of the pipette at bregma and set this point at X=0, Y=0.
Raise the pipette and place it on the X and Y coordinates of the targeted area for mPFC.
Scratch softly on the surface of the skull with forceps at each marked position.
Drill the skull to create a hole at the marked positions.
Apply pressure to the skull with the drill until you feel a drop-in resistance, indicating access to the brain.
If bleeding occurs, use cotton buds and saline solution to stop it.
Place the tip of the needle at the top of the hole and move down in the Z axis until reaching the surface of the brain.
Set the Z axis to 0 and take the Z coordinate for injection starting point (e.g., Z = −2.5).
Set the injection speed to 70 nl min−1.
Start the viral injection at the specified Z coordinate.
Make 70 nl steps along the Z axis in coordinates: −2.5, −2.3, −2.1, −1.9, −1.7, −1.5, −1.3 mm to cover the entire mPFC.
Inject a total volume of 500 nl of viral particles at each site.
Wait for 10 min before removing the pipette to avoid reflux and slowly withdraw it.
Check liquid is coming out of the tip under microscope before inserting the pipette into the brain to ensure it is not clogged.
Moisten the skin with a cotton bud and saline solution to help suture the skin.
Use 6.0 suture or skin glue to close the incision.
Apply antiseptic (betadine or similar), local anesthetics (lidocaine), and liquid glue after suturing to avoid the animal removing stitches.
Turn off anesthesia once surgery is complete.
Remove the ear bars and gas anesthesia mask from the animal.
Check the animal’s breathing and consciousness while keeping it in a heating pad post-surgery.
Place the animal in its cage with a heating pad below and monitor until regular breathing and locomotion are observed.
Administer buprenorphine (0.05 mL, 0.1 mg/mL) once daily for 48 hours after surgery to manage pain.
Monitor the mouse’s breathing during surgical procedures to adjust anesthesia levels appropriately.
Ensure that breathing is regular and without gasping throughout the procedure.
Infect astrocytes with AAV2.5-GFAP-Cre-mCherry between 3 and 5 weeks after viral expression begins.
Analyze the presence of knockout allele following Cre-mediated deletion of exon 7 and exon 8 by quantifying Gabbr1 and Gabbr2 gene expression in astrocytes.
Perform quantitative western blots to analyze protein levels in transfected astrocytes using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) from mPFC tissue.
Analyze mRNA levels of Gabbr1 and Gabbr2 by RT-qPCR.
Look at GABAB puncta located at the astrocytic membrane by immunohistochemical labeling.
Collect cells with a patch-clamp pipette under a fluorescence microscope to guide the selection of transfected astrocytes by mCherry reporter protein expression.
Extract RNA using magnetic beads from the collected astrocytic sample in lysis buffer.
Prepare cDNA library from the extracted RNA.
Prepare reaction mix for PCR and run qRT-PCR assay.
Acquire amplification results.
Collect cells from cortical slices for Magnetic Bead Purification of RNA and RT-qPCR.
Anesthetize control mice and GFAP/PFCΔGb animals with sodium pentobarbital 50 mg/kg, administered intraperitoneally.
Check for the absence of reflex in anesthetized mice.
Transcardially perfuse animals with NMDG-HEPES solution at 4°C using a 10 mL syringe.
Decapitate the mouse using scissors or a guillotine.
Cut the skin to expose the skull using fine scissors.
Make two horizontal cuts through the jaw bones.
Cut the skull along the midline carefully not to damage the brain.
Make a cut at the olfactory bulbs.
From the caudal midline, grab one half of the skull with forceps and open it to expose the brain. Then do it with the other half.
Extract the brain with a spatula from the ventral zone of the olfactory bulbs.
Slice the brain at 350 μm with NMDG-HEPES solution at 4°C using a vibratome.
Place the mPFC slices in a chamber with NMDG-HEPES at 37°C for 10 min.
Place the slices into a chamber with aCSF at RT (21°C–23°C) for the rest of the experiment.
Transfer slices to the recording chamber of the microscope in aCSF after 45–60 min.
Use a 40X/60X objective, CCD camera, illumination system, and software to identify mCherry-positive astrocytes based on fluorescence signal.
Fill borosilicate glass pipette with 2–3 μL of Lysis buffer 1x.
Approach the identified mCherry-positive astrocyte slowly without applying negative pressure.
Touch the membrane of the astrocyte with the pipette filled with lysis buffer.
Apply gentle negative pressure to follow a cell-attach configuration.
Move up the tip of the pipette slowly, ensuring that the cell follows and detaches from tissue.
Once detached, apply gentle negative pressure to incorporate intracellular content into the glass pipette.
Remove the pipette carefully from the headstage.
Break the tip of the pipette into vials containing 45 μL lysis buffer.
Collect cells directly into vial containing lysis buffer.
Close the vial and keep in dry ice.
Repeat collection process for 20–25 cells, adding each batch to the same vial.
Perform quick spin down of the vial with collected cells.
Incubate the vial at 65°C for 15 min in a water bath.
Spin down the vial after incubation to recover possible drops formed.
Store samples at -20°C or -80°C until processing.
Isolate RNA from cell lysates using magnetic beads according to DireCtQuant 100ST protocol.
Perform complementary DNA synthesis, library preparation and amplification following Pico Profiling workflow with Whole Transcriptome Amplification (WTA).
Add SYBR Green to the amplification reaction to monitor efficiency in real-time.
Stop the amplification reaction once the SYBR Green signal reaches a plateau.
Prepare cDNA mix for PCR amplification and divide it into three equivalent parts for technical replicates.
Include a sample without RNA as a control.
Purify cDNA using a PureLink Quick PCR Purification kit and elute in 40 μL of milliQ water.
Obtain the concentration of purified cDNA with a Nanodrop 1000 spectrophotometer.

Use primer sets to analyze Gabbr1 and Gabbr2 expression for qPCR: forward (ACAGACCAAATCTACCGGGC) and reverse (GTGCTGTCGTAGTAGCCGAT) for Gabbr1; forward (AAGCTCAAGGGGAACGACG) and reverse (ACTTGCTGCCAAACATGCTC) for Gabbr2.

Fill the wells of a hard-shell 384-well white well clear shell PCR plate with 5 μL of Sso Fast EvaGreen Supermix, 1 μL of primer mix (5 μM each), and 5 ng of pre-amplified cDNA to reach a total volume of 10 μL per well.
Anesthetize the animal with sodium pentobarbital 50 mg/kg, administered intraperitoneally.
Transcardially perfuse the animal with 10 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Follow by perfusing 40 mL PFA 4%.
Keep the brain in PFA 4% overnight.
If the brain is not analyzed immediately, saturate it in sucrose gradient solutions (7%, 32%), shaking at 4°C.
Store the saturated brain in cryoprotected solution (glycerol 3%) and ethylene glycol 3% in PBS.
Use a vibratome to cut the brain into 50 μm coronal slices.
Collect the slices in PBS in a multiwell plate.
Wash the slices three times for 20 minutes each with PBS.
Block non-specific binding with PBS containing 1% goat serum and 0.3% Triton-X 100 for 1 hour (blocking solution).
Incubate the slices with primary antibodies in blocking solution overnight at 4°C.
Wash the slices three times for 20 minutes each with blocking solution.
Incubate the slices with secondary antibodies in blocking solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the slices three times for 20 minutes each with 0.1% Triton/PBS.
Wash the slices three times for 20 minutes each with PBS.
Mount the slices using Vectashield antifade mounting medium.
Acquire 1 μm single optical sections using a x63 objective (1.40 NA, oil-inmersion) at 2,048 × 2,048 resolution with a confocal microscope.
Take Z-stack images of 7 μm in thickness containing mCherry-Cre/Cyto-GCaMP6f positive astrocytes in PFC using LAS X (Leica Application Suite X) software.
Open the z-stack images with ImageJ to analyze colocalization of mCherry-Cre/Cyto-GCaMP6f with S100 and NeuN labeling in the Z-stack images.
Select the channel of the infection (mCherry-Cre or Cyto-GCaMP6f) from the desired image file containing the z-stack maximum projection image.
Use the ROI manager tool in Fiji to select manually the fluorescent somatic regions.
Once all the ROIs are selected, press More in the ROI manager window and select OR (combine).
Create a mask that will be superimposed to the other channels to analyze co-localization by clicking on Edit → Selection → Create mask.
Click on Edit → Selection → Create Selection.
Press Shift+E.
Select the S100 channel window by clicking in it.
Add 3 more ROIs drawn in the S100 channel.
Select the NeuN channel window by clicking in it.
Add 3 more ROIs drawn in the NeuN channel.
Click on Measure in the ROI manager window for each channel.
Tag positive ROIs with 1 and negative ROIs with 0 for S100.
Calculate the percentage of positive ROIs for S100.
Tag positive ROIs with 1 and negative ROIs with 0 for NeuN.
Calculate the percentage of positive ROIs for NeuN.
Demarcate astrocyte somata and projections in the S100 channel using the ROI manager tool only in mCherry-positive astrocytes.
Create a mask from demarcated areas.
Paste the created mask into the GABABR channel.
Measure the GABABR intensity in these ROIs.
Analyze the puncta density at ROIs.
Obtain binary images from astrocytes using a threshold of 25–255.
Acquire the number of puncta using Analyze Particles in ImageJ.
Calculate the puncta density as the number of puncta versus ROI area.
Sacrifice control and GFAP/PFCΔGb mice 3–5 weeks after AAV2.5-GFAP-Cre-mCherry and AAV2.5-hGFAP-cyto-GCaMP6f injections.
Prepare mPFC slices as previously described.
Incubate the slices in aCSF at room temperature for 1 hour.
Transfer the slices to the chamber of the microscope (Nikon Eclipse FN1).
Isolate calcium-driven GABAergic responses using tetrodotoxin (TTX, 1 μM) and antagonists including D-AP5 (50 µM), CNQX (10 µM), AM251 (2 µM), MPEP (50 µM), and LY367385 (100 µM).
Identify GCaMP6f-positive astrocytes using a 40X-water immersion objective with 488 nm excitation wavelength.
Apply baclofen (2 mM) for 5 seconds via a pressure micro-injector placed close to the recorded astrocytes.
Record 2–3 minutes of video of calcium dynamics images using NIS-Elements Software or similar.
Use ATP (1 mM) local air puff as positive control to test viability of the astrocytes for GFAP/PFCΔGb mice, when no baclofen response is observed.
Perform time-lapse image-series analysis using ImageJ of the Fiji software.
Open video with ImageJ in AVI format.
Correct the x-y drift if needed with Turboreg plugin in ImageJ.
Define ROIs automatically by using MATLAB based software Caltracer3.

Extract time traces of fluorescence intensity of each ROI and convert it to ΔF/F values, where ΔF/F0 = (F(t) - F0)/(F0), being F0 the baseline fluorescence defined as the average minimum fluorescence across pre-stimulus frames.
Consider a calcium event when the fluorescence signal shows maximum values above three times the standard deviation of mean values of pre-stimulus frames.
Maintain GFAP/PFCΔGb mice and control mice (GABAB flox−/−) under food restriction above 80-85% of baseline body weights.
Deprive mice of water for 12 hours before behavioral sessions.
Keep the temperature at 23 ± 2°C and humidity at 55 ± 5% in experimental rooms.
Transfer mice to testing room at least 30 minutes before performing behavioral task.
Habituate mice to T-maze by placing them in maze for 15 minutes over a 3-day period.
Perform behavioral trials, each consisting of one sample run and one test run.
Block one side of the T arm with a wooden block during sample runs.
Place 0.1 ml reward (water or condensed milk) at the end of the opened arm.
Release mouse into start arm to enter the opened arm containing the reward.
Use a pseudorandom sequence to choose which arm to block, ensuring equal numbers of left and right turns per session and no more than two consecutive turns in the same direction.
Leave the mouse for 15 seconds at the beginning of the start arm, in a compartment separated by a door.
Remove the block and place the reward at the previously unvisited arm.
Open the door to allow the mouse to start the test.
Note the decision made by the animal (alternation or not alternation).
Consider an entry when the mouse has placed all four paws into the arm.
Repeat the trial 10 times per day for 6 days, with each trial separated by an inter-trial-interval of 5 minutes.
